name: Bodysurf a wave
blurb: Riding a wave with nothing but your body. It teaches you to read waves better than a board does, and it needs no equipment beyond a pair of fins.
gear: Swim fins — bodysurfing is very hard without them
A beach with clean, rolling waves
steps: Pick your wave: you want one just about to break, not one already broken.
Swim hard towards shore as it reaches you, matching its speed before it arrives.
At the moment it picks you up, extend one arm forward and drop that shoulder, turning your body into a planing surface.
Arch your back and keep your head up so your chest stays on the surface.
Learn to ride along the face at an angle rather than straight to the beach.
Learn to bail: tuck and roll rather than letting a wave drive you head-first into sand.
tips: Shore break on a steep beach can break necks. Learn on gentle, sloping beaches.
Fins do most of the work of catching the wave. Without them you will rarely get in early enough.
proof: Three rides in one session where you travel along the wave rather than straight in.
